meta.title: Dispatch Copilot: launch decision and pricing
meta.subtitle: Discussion document for the CEO and executive team, January 2027 planning
meta.purpose: Decide whether to launch Dispatch Copilot in Q2 2027, and how to package and price it
meta.confidentiality: Synthetic benchmark data: fictional company, every number from the briefing pack

inputs.label: Choices made by the team while the user was unavailable
inputs.content: Mode deck_detailed; audience CEO and exec team deciding; theme navy; storyline built as drafted; Pro allowance 1,000 requests per seat and overage priced at the 75% margin floor; Copilot engineers assumed to work Q1–Q2 2027; churned accounts assumed average size; the $0.6M platform cost treated as cost of revenue

storyline.governing_thought: Launch Copilot in Q2 2027 inside a Pro plan at $12 more per seat, not as a $149 add-on, and plan on about $2.9M of ARR, not $8M

exec_summary.text: Copilot creates real value, but less than the internal case claims

sub_points.text: Beta productivity rose 11% against 2% for matched accounts, among volunteers
AI costs at most $642K of new ARR a year in Routewise deals

exec_summary.text: As a $149 add-on, Copilot would sell to one account in seven and earn least on heavy users

sub_points.text: Only 14% paid when asked, against 46% in the survey
That gives about $2.5M of ARR, under a third of the $8M case

exec_summary.text: A Pro plan at $12 more per seat earns more, keeps margin and closes the NRR gap

sub_points.text: If 33% move up, as in 2023, Pro adds 5 percentage points of NRR
A usage allowance keeps company gross margin at 76.5%

exec_summary.text: A Q2 launch costs two more quarters of mobile churn, worth paying unless the rewrite fixes most of it

sub_points.text: Mobile reliability drives 4.5 times as much churn as AI features
Copilot first wins unless the rewrite removes over half of mobile churn

exec_summary.text: Launch on four conditions: a tested gain, a usage allowance, 26% Pro uptake and an early mobile restart

next_steps.action: Size how much mobile-reliability churn the rewrite would remove, against the break-even of about half (51.7%)
next_steps.owner: Head of Customer Success and mobile lead

next_steps.action: Run Copilot on randomly chosen non-beta accounts and compare jobs per dispatcher-hour with matched accounts
Set Pro pricing, the 1,000-request allowance and overage, and the migration offer for Core accounts
Check whether any of the 14 Copilot engineers can come from work other than the mobile rewrite
Renegotiate the inference contract before the fixed price ends

sections.title: Copilot's value is real but smaller than claimed

lead_message.text: Copilot lifted dispatcher productivity by 9 percentage points over matched accounts, though volunteers flatter the gain

slides.rationale: One claim (value is real but overstated), two beta measures -> two panels, no arrow

panels.header: Beta accounts scheduled far more jobs per dispatcher-hour than matched accounts
panels.unit_line: **Jobs per dispatcher-hour**, % change against the prior 12 weeks

panels.header: They also renewed more often, but volunteers are the accounts most likely to renew anyway
panels.unit_line: **Renewal rate**, % of accounts renewing within 90 days

slides.so_what: Treat the beta gain as a ceiling until a Q1 2027 test on randomly chosen accounts confirms it
footnotes: Beta: 240 volunteer accounts over 12 weeks, averaging 8.1 seats against 6.2 for all accounts and more active than the base; dispatchers also self-reported 4.1 hours saved a week
Matched non-beta accounts are Brightwork's own comparison group; the briefing pack does not say on which traits they were matched

lead_message.text: AI costs at most $642K of new ARR a year in Routewise deals, even if it caused the whole win-rate drop

slides.rationale: Win rate before and after Routewise's AI, plus the rate the memo implies -> columns with a sizing basis strip

sidebar.header: The sales memo overstates what AI is worth in deals

rows.label: Most new ARR a year at stake if AI caused all of the drop
rows.basis: 1,560 contested deals × 7 pp drop × $5,878 ARR per new account

footnotes: The memo rests on 31% of Q3 loss notes mentioning AI: a count of mentions across all lost deals, not of reasons in Routewise deals
"Implied by sales memo": the VP Sales claim that Copilot would recover a third of the deals lost to Routewise, applied to the 63% of contested deals lost in Q3 2026
